problem: The chapter says a mesh current is a real branch current only in branches 'on the outer edge'. That is not the criterion. The criterion is a branch that belongs to one mesh only. A branch that is not shared with another mesh (for example a dangling branch attached to an interior node) carries the mesh current but is not on the outer edge of the drawing.
fix: A mesh current equals the real branch current only in branches that belong to that mesh alone, that is, branches not shared with another mesh. In every shared branch the real current is the difference of the two mesh currents.

problem: 'the real current is the difference (or sum) of the two mesh currents' contradicts the rule stated earlier. With all mesh currents drawn clockwise, the two contributions in a shared branch always oppose, so the branch current is always the difference.
fix: In any shared branch the real current is the difference of the two clockwise mesh currents, i₁ − i₂; its sign tells you which way it actually flows.

problem: 'write them as a resistance matrix times a current vector equals a source vector' is true only for mesh analysis. Node analysis gives a conductance matrix times a node-voltage vector equals a current-source vector.
fix: Mesh analysis gives [R][i] = [V], a resistance matrix times a mesh-current vector equals a source-voltage vector. Node analysis gives [G][V] = [I], a conductance matrix times a node-voltage vector equals a source-current vector.

problem: With show_index true and index_from 1, the mark key '1' points at the first column, so the accent falls on 6 in row 1 and on −4 in row 2. The caption says the accent is on the two shared 4 Ω terms, which are in the second column.
fix: Set marks to {'2': 'accent'} in both rows so the highlighted column is −4 and −4, the shared-resistance terms.

problem: 'Every circuit simulator builds these same matrices internally' overstates the case: simulators use node-based modified nodal analysis, not mesh analysis, as the Beyond note itself says.
fix: Circuit simulators build the node equations (in modified form) internally; mesh analysis stays a hand method.
